Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: In Spring 1908, the regents appointed John W. Gilmore, professor of agriculture at ___E:Cornell University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University)___ , as the college's first president.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#19

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#20

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#21
Main.sentence: In September 1912 it moved to its present location in Mānoa Valley on 90 acres of land that had been cobbled together from leased and private lands and was renamed the College of Hawaii.

Main.sentence: William Kwai Fong Yap, a cashier at ___E:Bank of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Hawaii)___ , and a group of citizens petitioned the ___E:Hawaii Territorial Legislature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_Territorial_Legislature)___ six years later for university status which led to another renaming finally to the University of Hawaiʻi on April 30, 1919, with the addition of the College of Arts and Sciences and College of Applied Science.

Main.sentence: In the years following, the university expanded to include more than 300 acres.

Main.sentence: In 1931 the Territorial ___E:Normal School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_school)___ was absorbed into the university, becoming Teacher's College,  now the College of Education.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#25
Main.sentence: The university continued its growth throughout the 1930s and 1940s increasing from 232 to 402 acres.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#27
Main.sentence: The university's ROTC program was put into active duty, which made the campus resemble a military school.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#28
Main.sentence: When classes resumed on February 11, 1942, about half of the student and faculty body left to enter the war or military service.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#29
Main.sentence: Students who returned to campus found classes cancelled due to lack of faculty and were required to carry gas masks to classes and bomb shelters were kept at a ready.

Main.sentence: Once the war was over, student enrollment grew faster than the university had faculty and space for.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#31
Main.sentence: In 1947, the university opened an extension center in Hilo on Hawaiʻi Island in the old Hilo Boarding School.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#32
Main.sentence: In 1951, Hilo Center was designated the University of Hawaii Hilo Branch  before its reorganization by an act of the Hawaiʻi State Legislature in 1970.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#33
Main.sentence: By the 1950s, enrollment increased to more than 5,000 students, and the university had expanded to include a Graduate Division, College of Education, College of Engineering, College of Business Administration, College of Tropical Agriculture, and College of Arts and Sciences.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#34
Main.sentence: When Hawaiʻi was granted statehood in 1959, the university became a constitutional agency rather than a legislative agency with the Board of Regents having oversight over the university.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#35
Main.sentence: Enrollment continued to grow to 19,000 at the university through the 1960s and the campus became nationally recognized in research and graduate education.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#36
Main.sentence: In 1965, the state legislature created a system of community colleges and placed it within the university at the recommendations of the ___E:Department of Health, Education and Welfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Health,_Education_and_Welfare)___ 's report on higher education in Hawaii and UH President Thomas H. Hamilton.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#37
Main.sentence: By the end of the 1960s, the University of Hawaiʻi was very different from what it had since its beginning.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#38
Main.sentence: It had become larger and with the addition of the community colleges, a broad range of activities extending from vocational education to community college education, which were all advanced through research and postdoctoral training.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#39
Main.sentence: The university was renamed the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa to distinguish it from other campuses in the University of Hawaiʻi System in 1972.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#40
Main.sentence: The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa operates within the University of Hawaiʻi System, which is governed by an 11-member board of regents who are nominated by the Regents Candidate Advisory Council, appointed by the governor, and confirmed by the State of Hawaiʻi legislature.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#41
Main.sentence: The board also appoints the president of the University of Hawaiʻi System, who provides leadership for all 10 campuses, including as the chief executive of UH Mānoa.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#42
Main.sentence: Day-to-day academic and operational management of UH Mānoa is the responsibility of the Provost.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#43
Main.sentence: When UH began as the College of Hawaiʻi, Willis T. Pope served as acting dean from 1907 to 1908, despite declining the title of "acting president." Since that initial period, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa has always been led by a president, chancellor, or provost, including interim or acting roles.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#44
Main.sentence: From 1908 to 1965, the president of the University of Hawaiʻi, before the creation of the University of Hawaii System (UH System), served as chief executive of the university.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#45
Main.sentence: Technical and community colleges and Hilo College operated separately from what would later become the UH System.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#46
Main.sentence: In 1965 the ___E:Hawaiʻi State Legislature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawai%CA%BBi_State_Legislature)___ created the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_System)___ , which incorporated the technical and community colleges into the university.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#47
Main.sentence: The President's role was expanded to include oversight of the new university system.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#48
Main.sentence: In 1974, the role of chancellor was established to handle campus-specific leadership, allowing the UH President to focus on system-wide governance.

Main.sentence: In 2001, the position of chancellor was re-established by UH System president ___E:Evan Dobelle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Dobelle)___ over ___E:conflict of interest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict_of_interest)___ concerns.

Main.sentence: Presidents

Main.sentence: The Provost role was established to handle the academic and operational affairs of UH Mānoa, while the President served as the chief executive of the university and retained overall UH System leadership.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#55
Main.sentence: This reorganization was made to create a governance structure similar to other major research universities, such as the University of Washington and Indiana University.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#57
Main.sentence: UH Mānoa, the flagship campus of the University of Hawaiʻi System, is a four-year research university consisting of 17 schools and colleges.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#58
Main.sentence: In addition to undergraduate and graduate degrees in the School of Architecture, School of Earth Science and Technology, the College of Arts, Languages, and Letters, the ___E:Shidler College of Business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shidler_College_of_Business)___ , the College of Education, and the College of Engineering, the university also maintains professional schools in law and medicine.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#59
Main.sentence: Together, the colleges and schools of the university offer bachelor's degrees in 93 fields of study, master's degrees in 84 fields, doctoral degrees in 51 fields, first professional degrees in five fields, post-baccalaureate degrees in three fields, 28 undergraduate certification programs, and 29 graduate certification programs.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#60
Main.sentence: Originally called the College of Agriculture and Mechanic Arts of the Territory of Hawaiʻi and formerly the College of Applied Sciences, the College of Tropical Agriculture & Human Resources (CTAHR) is the founding college of the university.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#61
Main.sentence: Programs of the college focuses on ___E:tropical agriculture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_agriculture)___ , ___E:food science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_science)___ and human nutrition, textiles and clothing, and Human Resources.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#62
Main.sentence: The name of the college was changed in October 2024 to the College of Tropical Agriculture & Human Resilience.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#63
Main.sentence: The college was established as the Honolulu Training School in 1895 to prepare and train teachers and then Territorial Normal and Training School after Hawaiʻi became a territory in 1905.  As the school outgrew its location on the ___E:Punchbowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punchbowl_Crater)___ side of Honolulu, a new campus was to be constructed on the corner of University Avenue and Metcalf Street.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#64
Main.sentence: The first two buildings constructed by the Territorial Department of Public instruction became known as Wist Hall and Wist Annex 1.  The normal school was eventually merged into the University of Hawaiʻi in 1931 as the Teacher's College.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#65
Main.sentence: In 1959, the name was changed to the College of Education.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#66
Main.sentence: The College of Arts, Languages, and Letters (CALL) is the newest and largest college at the university.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#67
Main.sentence: It was created following the dissolution of the College of Arts and Science and the merger of the Colleges of Arts and Humanities, Languages, Linguistics, and Literature (LLL) and the School of Pacific and Asian Studies.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#68
Main.sentence: The college's core focus is the study of arts, humanities, and languages with a particular focus on Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia Studies.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#69
Main.sentence: The College of Business Administration was established in 1949 with programs in accounting, finance, real estate, industrial relations, and marketing.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#70
Main.sentence: The college was renamed the Shidler College of Business on September 6, 2006, after real-estate executive Jay Shidler, an alumnus of the college, who donated $25 million to the college.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#71
Main.sentence: The School of Nursing was established in 1951, even though courses in nursing had been offered since 1932 with a partnership with Queen's Hospital School of Nursing.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#72
Main.sentence: The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa Library, which provides access to 3.4 million volumes, 50,000 journals, and thousands of digitized documents, is one of the largest academic research libraries in the United States, ranking 86th in parent institution investment among 113 North American members of the Association of Research Libraries.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#73
Main.sentence: The UH Mānoa offers an Honors Program to provide additional resources for students preparing to apply to ___E:professional school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_school)___ programs.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#74
Main.sentence: Students complete core curriculum courses for their degrees in the Honors Program, maintain at least a cumulative 3.2 ___E:grade-point average U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grading_in_education)___ in all courses, and complete a senior thesis project.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#75
Main.sentence: The National Science Foundation ranked UH Mānoa 45th among 395 public universities for Research and Development (R&D) expenditures in fiscal year 2014.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#76
Main.sentence: According to U.S.

Main.sentence: News & World Report ' s rankings for 2021, UH Mānoa was tied at 170th overall and 159th for "Best Value" among national universities; tied at 83rd among public universities; and tied at 145th for its undergraduate engineering program among schools that confer doctorates.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#78
Main.sentence: The university offers over 50 ___E:distance learning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_education)___ courses, using technology to replace either all or a portion of class instruction.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#79
Main.sentence: Students interact with their instructors and peers from different locations to further develop their education.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#80
Main.sentence: With extramural grants and contracts of $436 million in 2012, research at UH Mānoa relates to Hawaii's physical landscape, its people and their heritage.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#81
Main.sentence: The geography facilitates advances in marine biology, oceanography, underwater robotic technology, astronomy, geology and geophysics, agriculture, aquaculture and tropical medicine.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#82
Main.sentence: Its heritage, the people and its close ties to the Asian and Pacific region create a favorable environment for study and research in the arts, genetics, intercultural relations, linguistics, religion and philosophy.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#83
Main.sentence: According to the ___E:National Science Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation)___ , UH Mānoa spent $276 million on research and development in 2018, ranking it 84th in the nation.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#84
Main.sentence: Extramural funding increased from $368 million in FY 2008 to nearly $436 million in FY 2012. Research grants increased from $278 million in FY 2008 to $317 million in FY 2012. Non-research awards totaled $119 million in FY 2012. Overall, extramural funding increased by 18%.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#85
Main.sentence: For the period of July 1, 2012 to June 20, 2013, the ___E:School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Ocean_and_Earth_Science_and_Technology)___ (SOEST) received the largest amount of extramural funding among the Mānoa units at $92 million.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#86
Main.sentence: SOEST was followed by the medical school at $57 million, the College of Natural Sciences and the University of Hawaiʻi Cancer Center at $24 million, the ___E:Institute for Astronomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Astronomy_(Hawaii))___ at $22 million, CTARH at $18 million, and the College of Social Sciences and the College of Education at $16 million.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#87
Main.sentence: Across the UH system, the majority of research funding comes from the ___E:Department of Health and Human Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health_and_Human_Services)___ , the ___E:Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ , the ___E:Department of Education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education)___ , the ___E:National Science Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation)___ , the ___E:Department of Commerce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce)___ , and the ___E:National Aeronautics Space Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA)___ (NASA).

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#88
Main.sentence: Local funding comes from Hawaii government agencies, non-profit organizations, health organizations and business and other interests.

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#89
Main.sentence: The $150-million medical complex in Kakaʻako opened in the spring of 2005. The facility houses a biomedical research and education center that attracts significant federal funding and private sector investment in biotechnology and cancer research and development. [citation needed]

Main.id: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa - Wikipedia#90
Main.sentence: Research (broadly conceived) is expected of every faculty member at UH Mānoa.
